title: Grove caps inflows to every Centrifuge instance but leaves outflows unlimited, so risk controls never impede exit
content:
The pattern holds across every instance documented in this chunk. Centrifuge JTRSY: inflow 500,000,000 USDC with a 500,000,000-per-day slope, outflow `Unlimited` (A...3.1.1.1.2.4.1–2). Centrifuge JAAA: inflow 100,000,000 with a 50,000,000-per-day slope, outflow `Unlimited` (A...3.1.1.2.2.4.1–2). Centrifuge ACRDX: deposit 20,000,000 with a 20,000,000-per-day slope, withdrawal `Unlimited` (A...3.1.1.3.2.4.1–2). Centrifuge JTRSY USDS Vault: inflow 500,000,000 USDS, outflow `Unlimited` (A...3.1.1.4.2.4.1–2).

The asymmetry encodes a principle that is easy to state and easy to get wrong: **a rate limit is a control on taking risk, not a control on activity.** Throttling withdrawals would throttle de-risking, and would bind hardest in exactly the scenario the limits exist to survive — a counterparty deteriorating while Grove tries to get out.

It also composes with the emergency protocol in A...2.2.3.2, which instructs an operator to redeem *all* positions and centralise liquidity in the proxy. That instruction is only executable because no outflow limit stands in its way; a symmetric limit design would have made the documented emergency procedure impossible to complete in one action.

The cost accepted is that a compromised relayer can pull everything out of a protocol in one transaction. Grove judges that acceptable because the funds land in the ALM Proxy, not with the attacker — the proxy is the safe destination, so unlimited movement *toward* it is not an exposure.
description: Each instance config pairs a finite inflow maxAmount and slope with an outflow maxAmount of Unlimited — throttling only the direction that increases exposure.
